No introduced security concern was established, but the assessment is limited to the reviewed source paths. **Retained concerns** No architecture-level concerns identified.

Event validation rejects inverted ranges before writing. Time-entry database functions bind ownership to app_user_id(), validate ranges and restrict changes to running timers. These inspected downstream controls are unchanged by the PR. **Resilience and Maintainability Implications** - _observed_ — Existing failure-containment mechanisms remain in the changed producers' persistence paths: event updates use version conflicts and explicit reload or overwrite choices; time-entry updates lock the owned row, compare versions and record the prior value transactionally. Manual creates deduplicate by authenticated user and request ID. These controls bound concurrent edits and retries after an uncertain response without relying on DST selection state.
